text: I bought this mini-washer to get by when my regular washer was down and waiting for service, which happens about once per year.  It can take up to two weeks to get it fixed, after troubleshooting, ordering parts, installing parts.  Takes too long.  There are some downfalls to this product, but I knew I was buying a mini-washer for about $120.00 to serve as a back-up.  It does very little automatically.  You have to turn the water on to fill the machine.  You have to turn a dial to empty the tub.  You have to manually place the clothes into the spin cycle and manually add water during the spin rinse.  But, you don't have to wash your clothes by hand just because the main washer is out-of-service.  This machine was a Godsend.  What it does well is wash clothes.  So with a little extra effort, the end game goals are met nicely by this machine.  It was easy to unpack, set up, and learn to use.  The only other real downside is that I cannot imagine washing more than two bath towels at a time.  The spin compartment is just not large enough.  Overall, this serves my purpose really well and works better than I had imagined.  If I was in a college dorm room, or some other area where I could not put a washer, this would make me happy.

I have to say I have been impressed so far! It holds more laundry than I anticipated (about 1/3 a normal size load) though I have been careful not to overload it and stress the machine. The agitator is powerful and removes way more dirt than our community laundry machines (makes me feel a little gross about what we've been wearing)!

I did about 13-14 loads of laundry yesterday, so I feel like I've got a pretty good feel for what this little machine can do. The set up was super easy once I figured out where to put it. The inlet hose for our bathroom sink perfectly, though I have read other users had issues with the fit. I simply ran the drain hose into our toilet (after a good bleach down, of course).

I chose to use the spin/rinse features together rather than rinsing in the agitator side. This worked perfectly! I set the spin timer for 3 minutes and ran the water into that side for about two them turned it off and let the rest spin out for about a minute. The clothes came out super clean and about 75% dry.

I first bought this little washer back in 2016 when I moved into an RV.  The first one I got had issues with spinning after three months, but the manufacturer stood behind it and replaced it. I noticed that this one was much shorter than the old one, which made it harder to use (since it sat at knee level) so I set it on the styrofoam that it was packaged in to raise it a couple of inches, and did my laundry.  At that point I noticed that the new tub was smaller and the spinner is MUCH smaller than the one I had before.  The agitation and spinner seems to be stronger, but the smaller capacity is going to be a problem.  I can only fit one sweatshirt in the spinner, and I had to do three loads instead of two because of the smaller tub.  Also it is slow to drain (this was an issue with the old one as well) and I have to tip it to get the pump to engage and fully drain it.  Altogether I am not impressed with the new design.

We bought this for our apartment. We have enough space for a full washer and dryer, but not the funds for one. This does more than expected. We can even wash towels! For the last week we've been catching up on some laundry, doing a few loads in the evening and hanging them to dry overnight.

A few tips:
Leave the covers open after you're finished doing laundry, and run the "drain" cycle again to make sure it's empty.
The spinner dries clothes pretty efficiently, two minutes of not adding water to it will give a big boost to dry time.
The pump isn't super powerful, make sure the hose is draining into something that's at the same level or lower than the machine. We have been using our bathtub, and storing it in the closet when not in use.

My daughter called whining about having to go to the laundromat. After explaining to her that washing machines are expensive and that I don't have that kind of money I volunteered to help her find something. There was a big catch. It had to be less than 27in wide. My Bosch front loader is less than 27in wide, but that wasn't going to happen for her. So I searched Lowe's to see what brands I should look for at the used place, the only ones that size were Bosch and commercial grade washers. They would even be too expensive used. I decided to check Amazon just to see if there was some brand I'd never heard of and low and behold I discovered this style of washing machines. I remember when I used to live in an apartment and I would've killed for something like this. I read the reviews and decided to give it a try. I got it today and tried it out just to see how it works. It is amazing. It works great. I was worried about the drain, but you have to manually select the drain (unless its on spin) so it doesn't just randomly spit out water like a regular washing machine. The spin got the clothes just as dry as the Bosch so they should line dry overnight. For an apartment with one or two people, its way better (and cheaper) than schlepping laundry to the laundromat. Its also pretty light. Don't know how long it'll last, but if it makes it more than 3 months it'll be worth it.
